steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour two 8-inch round cake pans.
In a measuring cup, combine milk, 1/2 cup orange juice, oil, beaten eggs, and 1 1/2 teaspoon orange zest. Set aside.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder into a large bowl. Mix in sugar. Make a well in the center and pour in the milk mixture. Stir until thoroughly combined.
Divide batter into prepared pans. Bake in the preheated oven for 35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean. Allow to cool.

To make Orange Butter Frosting: Cream butter until smooth. Gradually beat in confectioners' sugar. Beat until light and fluffy. Beat in 2 tablespoons orange juice to bring to spreading consistency. Stir in vanilla and 1 teaspoon orange zest.

raw_recipe.headline: Beat and Bake Orange Cake
raw_recipe.description: This quick orange cake is delicious without the frosting. I sometimes just sprinkle icing sugar on the top. This recipe can be used to make two 8-inch cake layers or a 9x5-inch loaf. If making a loaf cake, bake for 60 minutes.

review.reviewBody: Oh my goodness, I am SO glad I looked for a recipe today to use up a bunch of oranges! What a wonderful, lovely, delicious cake! I took a few suggestions from other reviewers and the result was perfect. I used 1 T. of zest and about 2 T. orange marmalade in the batter (tho' I don't know that the marmalade was really necessary). I made the cake in two 8-inch layers, and made the frosting as stated with just a little less vanilla than called for, which made enough to fill and frost the top. The orange flavor came through perfectly, the cake is moist and a beautiful shade of yellow-orange. The frosting is a must in my opinion, creamy and fluffy, and takes this cake over the top. I made this for my husband to take to the office tomorrow, but this cake is staying right here!

Ok so I followed this recipe to the letter, and even though I hade my mouth set for that creamy frosting my hubbz wanted a glaze. (One cup confectioners sugar, 1 tb spoon orange zest, 3 t-spoons oj... Adjust to your liking) OMG.... AMAZING!!! Will be making again!! Tips for the glaze... Put fork holes throughout the top.... I made in a bundt pan... And it needed about 90 minutes in the oven. But I poured the glaze while the cake was still hot and let it sit overnight.... Hubbz loved it!!

I made this cake for my cousin's birthday and it was delicious! Based on the reviews, I added 1 T. of orange zest and about 2 T. orange marmalade to the batter. I sprinkled orange juice on the finished cakes and they absorbed it very well making it moist. This cake is a little on the denser side, so I decided to frosted the cake with whipped cream-cream cheese frosting (with a couple of tablespoons of orange juice and 1 tsp of orange zest to make it more orangy). The light frosting went very well with the cake and the whole thing was beautiful!

This is a delicious cake! I made it for my mother in laws 87th birthday. I changed the steps in how the ingredients were blended using an electric hand mixer. Beat the eggs, add the oil, sugar, orange zest, orange juice (fresh squeezed). After measuring and combining the dry ingredients I added the dry ingredients to the wet in 3 portions alternating flour and milk. I used Almond milk instead of cow's milk. So moist and delicious!

I made this delicious cake in a 13"X9" Pyrex baking dish. Instead of the buttercream frosting, I made a simple orange glaze (powdered sugar, orange zest, and orange juice). When the cake was still just barely warm, I poked holes in it with a toothpick and slowly spread the glaze over the cake. Everyone loved this cake! Thanks for the recipe -- definitely a keeper!

Hello thank you for the Recipe, the cake came out delicious I used cuties brand oranges and added 2 cups regular white sugar and 2tsp orange extract I,I also added little less then 1/4 c. Orange marmalade that aided in the moisture ..the pool only. Bad side was that it took about 45 min to bake because I added in the extras.will be saving this recipe thanks:)

Very tasty and moist with a beautiful crumb! I baked my cake in a 9x13 pan which baked in 30 minutes. I used my Tupperware bowl and melted the butter in that fot the oil, then threw all the other cake ingredients in and beat for 2 minutes with my hand mixer. I doubled the zest and added 1/4 tsp orange oil. If you make layers I would double or triple the frosting as I just had enough to cover the top of the 9x13 cake. I didn't have any juice left for the frosting so I used cream and doubled the zest and added 1/4 tsp orange oil. Smells awesome in my house!

Excellent. Family loved it. Made in small glass pan with lid. Baked for 40 minutes ant 350. Added orange extract (1/2 tsp) to batter and made the frosting I used with grandson’s favourite lemon cupcakes except used vanilla pudding with orange extract.

I love this cake. I saw this recipe and decided to try something new and different. I am 100% happy with the way it turned out. I sprayed 2 round cake pans with baking spray. Then I used parchment paper. I sprayed the parchment paper then divided my batter. The cake came out of the pans perfectly. This cake is a very moist cake. The orange zest adds so much flavor. I did use more orange zest than the recipe called for. I happy I did. I highly recommend this delicious cake recipe. Thanks!! Sherry
I added extra orange zest and juice to both the cake and frosting, and the flavor turned out perfect! I have requests to make it again, so I will definitely be using this recipe again in the future!

Great recipe. I've always made this as written, but today I followed some reviewers advice and added 2 tbsp of triple sec and a 1/4 cup of sour cream to the batter (I also added some green and red jimmies to make it more Christmasy). I baked it in a bundt pan for 40 minutes then glazed it (1 1/4 c powdered sugar, 2 tbsp orange juice and 1/2 tsp vanilla.)

Made exactly as directed. Came out dense but not dry. I used fresh squeezed orange juice. Flavor was subtle and delicious. Next time I will do a glaze or drizzle. The frosting was too sweet & heavy for my liking.
Absolutely loved this recipe easy to follow and all my friends loved it couldn’t stop eating it, also note it was my first time baking a cake from scratch and it turned out amazing.
The cake was dry and tiny and I had to make a double batch of the icing. This was a very disappointing recipe.
Made this for my daughter's 14th Birthday 3months ago and now made twice since; making tomorrow! It freezes well too.
It was so moist. I did add more zest and orange flavoring only because my husband and I love the extra flavoring.
Everyone loved it. I'm making it again today for my husband's birthday. I also added 1/2 cup coconut to the batter. For the icing I also added a dash of milk and sprinkled with extra coconut. 😋

Very solid recipe, the only thing that went wrong was that the ingredients for icing and cake weren't separated so I just put it all together! haha I made a few changes myself as we are dairy free. Instead of milk I just did fresh blended oranges. I did 1c sugar and 1c powdered sugar but it wasn't actually to sweet as I didn't do any icing. I also put a table spoon zest in the cake. I made these into cupcakes instead of cake. they are super fluffy and moist with a nice bounce. Ill definitely be adding this recipe to my saved ones.

This cake is good. I added more orange juice and zest to the cake recipe as well as the frosting recipe. Next time I make this cake, I will buy some orange liqueur; as I think it will make it a five star cake. I also baked in two 9” cake pans and of course the cake was a little thinner due to the larger pans. Thanks for sharing your recipe.
I halved the recipe and used a cream cheese frosting recipe using granulated sugar. I made 12 little cakes and they are amazing!
